text:
liam (AE): MercuryTrust POC running into lots of 429s and some really high TTFT on small prompts. Customer says it looks fine locally but in our environment they're getting ~300-700ms TTFT and bursts of 429s. They're blocked on demos tomorrow. Can we assemble a quick triage?

sara (CS): Adding context: traffic is mostly single-turn chat messages, ~20-60 tokens. Non-streaming. They mentioned repeated identical prep-system prompts across sessions (probable cacheable). Any recent deploys to the routing layer?

kai (SRE): Pulling logs: seeing ratelimit decisions where tenant_rate_limit.window_tokens exhausted, then many client retries without backoff. Also a high kv_cache_miss rate for route=mercurytrust-poc which increases backend cost and exec_ms. Snippet: 

```
[ratelimit] tenant=mercurytrust burst_remaining=0 window_seconds=60
[worker-7] route=mercurytrust-poc enqueue_delay_ms=90 batch_size=1 exec_ms=380 http_status=429 err="rate_limited"
[caching] route=mercurytrust-poc kv_cache miss key=system_prompt_v2
```

kai (SRE): Hypothesis: three contributing factors 1) client retries amplifying load -> 429s, 2) high cache miss causing heavier model execs, 3) traffic pattern produces many single-request batches worsening TTFT.

ana (Ana?) Wait need to be consistent: ana is infra eng.

ana (Infra Eng): small correction :) For short chatty workloads we often enable response-prefix caching and a prefill path. For quick mitigation I can: 1) increase tenant burst tokens temporarily, 2) enable prefix_kv_cache for common system prompts, 3) lower batch_window_ms to 10 and cap max_batch_size=32. Example commands: 

```
redwoodctl tenants update --tenant mercurytrust --set burst_tokens=5000 --set refill_seconds=60
redwoodctl routes update --route mercurytrust-poc --set batch_window_ms=10 --set max_batch_size=32
redwoodctl cache enable --route mercurytrust-poc --type prefix_kv --ttl=600s
```

ana (Infra Eng): If they can't change client behavior, server-side prefill + small-window batching + caching should reduce TTFT a lot.

sara (CS): Deb 1) customer also sent a security questionnaire (SAML, data residency, logging), and finance asked about an upper spend cap for the POC. Can you weigh in?

deb (Security): Quick answers: SAML SSO supported for console; data residency options per-region; we push audit logs to customer SIEM via syslog/forwarder; per-route payload logs are redactable and can be disabled. For keys, we support customer-managed KMS; HSM on Private deployments. Nothing blocking for POC. I'll do the full form but no blockers for demo.

billing-bot: Noted. Current POC invoice: 0.00 USD so far. Standard internal POC credit: request via finance.

kai (SRE): I also see spikes in model_open_time when kv_cache misses. Prewarming small models with a keep-alive pool can help for POCs. Proposal: start a 2-node warm pool pinned to mercurytrust-poc model variant for 30 minutes during demos. It reduces cold-start exec_ms variance.

liam (AE): Can we do both warm-pool and the cache/route changes now? Customer wants a hard $3k cap for the POC and a daily alert at 50% spend.

ana (Infra Eng): Implementing route + cache changes now. Will also request temporary burst increase and provision warm-pool. Commands run: 

```
redwoodctl routes update --route mercurytrust-poc --set batch_window_ms=10 --set max_batch_size=32
redwoodctl cache enable --route mercurytrust-poc --type prefix_kv --ttl=600s
redwoodctl tenants update --tenant mercurytrust --set burst_tokens=5000
redwoodctl infra provision-warm-pool --route mercurytrust-poc --nodes=2 --duration=1800
```

redwood-deploy-bot: applied routes update by ana. warm-pool provisioning started: nodes_assigned=2 status=initializing -> ready.

kai (SRE): After changes: 429s dropped to near zero within 90s, kv_cache_miss_rate fell from 72% -> 18% for the sampled keys, median TTFT fell from 420ms -> 95ms. Still seeing tail spikes at 400ms when batch_size=1. Need client-side jitter or adaptive small-request path to fix tail.

liam (AE): I'll ask the MercuryTrust client if they can add a 10ms jitter + coalescing on their SDK. If they can't, can we flip adaptive small-request path? What's the risk?

ana (Infra Eng): adaptive_small_request_path reduces per-request overhead but slightly increases CPU overhead and can affect throughput at very high QPS. For a POC it's low risk. We can toggle for the route: 

```
redwoodctl routes update --route mercurytrust-poc --set adaptive_small_request_path=true
```

kai (SRE): My recommendation: 1) keep burst_tokens elevated during demo window, 2) keep prefix_kv_cache enabled, 3) ask client to implement 10ms jitter, 4) enable adaptive_small_request_path if client can't change SDK. Also set alerts to page on >80% spend of POC credit.

deb (Security): Security form: sent final draft to sara. Key points: logs redaction process, data retention 90d by default, optional extended retention, support for private deployment and HSM.

sara (CS): Finance approved a $3k credit for POC with daily spend alerts. I've configured billing alerts to @liam and @sara at 50% and 90%.

billing-bot: Billing alert configured: tenant=mercurytrust thresholds=[50,90] contacts=[liam,sara]. POC credit requested: 3000 USD pending finance approval.

kai (SRE): Ran a controlled replay simulating recommended client jitter + caching + adaptive path. Results: batch_size distribution improved (size=1 reduced by 60%), median TTFT 86ms, 95th percentile 165ms, kv_cache_hit_ratio >80% on cached keys. No 429s during 20m run. Will keep monitoring.

liam (AE): Great. I'll send MercuryTrust the technical summary, security responses, and confirmation of the $3k credit + spend alarms. Thanks team 1) closing for now, will reopen if anomalies reappear during their live demo tomorrow.
